stem: The student wants to emphasize the bridge's engineering achievement relative to earlier thin-arch bridges. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Vella River Footbridge was completed in 1931 in the town of Kestrel Falls.
• Engineer Hana Dvořáková designed it with reinforced concrete arches only 9 centimeters thick.
• At the time, most concrete arch bridges of similar span used arches at least 30 centimeters thick.
• Thin concrete arches had been built earlier in Switzerland, but those bridges required steel cable supports.
• Dvořáková's bridge was the first to span more than 40 meters with a thin concrete arch and no cable supports.
• The bridge still carries pedestrians today.
choices: Completed in 1931, Hana Dvořáková's Vella River Footbridge, whose concrete arches are only 9 centimeters thick, still carries pedestrians across the river today.
Dvořáková's bridge was the first to span more than 40 meters with a thin concrete arch alone, whereas earlier thin arches in Switzerland had required steel cable supports.
Dvořáková's 9-centimeter concrete arches were far thinner than the arches of at least 30 centimeters that were typical of similar bridges built at the time.
Unlike the earlier thin-arch bridges built in Switzerland, Dvořáková's bridge was the first ever to span more than 40 meters using a thin concrete arch.
explanation: The goal asks for an achievement measured against one comparison group: earlier thin-arch bridges. The note that makes the bridge matter is the 'first' note, and its significance depends on the Swiss bridges, which needed cable supports. Choice B gives the first, keeps the condition that makes it a first (no cable supports), and uses 'whereas' to name the contrast with those earlier thin arches.

A.why: You picked an accurate description: the date, the designer, how thin the arches are, and the fact that the bridge is still in use. None of it says why the bridge was an achievement, and it never mentions the earlier thin-arch bridges the goal asks you to compare it with.

C.why: You saw that the significance has to be relative, but you used the wrong comparison. This choice compares the bridge with typical thick-arch bridges. The goal asks about earlier thin-arch bridges, and the Swiss bridges' arches were probably thin as well, so this contrast doesn't do the job.

D.why: You went for the 'first' and the Swiss comparison but missed that this choice drops the condition that made the bridge a first: no cable supports. The notes never say the Swiss bridges spanned less than 40 meters. Without that condition, the choice claims a record the notes don't support.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the significance of Ibarra's findings in relation to what researchers had previously assumed. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Kelp forests can collapse when sea urchins overgraze them, leaving bare areas called urchin barrens.
• Researchers had long assumed that kelp returns to a barren only if urchin densities fall below about 2 per square meter.
• Marine ecologist Tomás Ibarra monitored 12 barrens off the coast of Chile for three years.
• In four barrens, kelp regrew even though urchin densities stayed above 6 per square meter.
• In those four barrens, urchins mostly sheltered in crevices and ate drifting kelp rather than grazing attached kelp.
• Ibarra concluded that urchin behavior, not just urchin numbers, can determine whether kelp recovers.
choices: Over three years, Ibarra monitored 12 urchin barrens off the coast of Chile, tracking urchin densities and recording where and how the urchins fed.
In four of the barrens Ibarra monitored, kelp regrew while urchin densities stayed above 6 per square meter and the urchins ate mostly drifting kelp.
Kelp regrew in four barrens with more than 6 urchins per square meter, well above the long-assumed threshold of 2, showing that urchin numbers play no role in recovery.
Kelp regrew in four barrens with more than 6 urchins per square meter, well above the long-assumed threshold of 2, suggesting that urchin behavior also shapes recovery.
explanation: The goal ties the findings to an earlier assumption, so the answer has to include that assumption. Regrowth at more than 6 urchins per square meter only matters because researchers expected kelp to return only below 2. Choice D sets the finding against that threshold and then states Ibarra's conclusion accurately: behavior matters as well as numbers.

A.why: You picked a description of the study's method: where Ibarra worked, for how long, and what he measured. It reports no finding and never mentions the earlier assumption, so it can't show why the results matter.

B.why: You found the key result, but here it is a bare fact. 'Above 6 per square meter' only shows significance next to the long-assumed threshold of 2, and this choice leaves that threshold out, so a reader can't tell the result overturned anything.

C.why: You correctly set the finding against the old threshold, then accepted a conclusion that goes too far. Ibarra concluded that behavior, 'not just urchin numbers,' matters. That means numbers still count. Saying they play 'no role' turns his conclusion into a stronger claim than he made.
